verdict.rationale: YYLO stores validated workflow definitions as typed records in its Git-native Ledger, saves workflow contracts as YAML, and documents independently versioned Skills that users should review before installing. That gives its automations a versioned, reviewable form. Nothing documents a first-class review flow for workflow changes or any rollback or revert mechanism for automations; versioning appears to rest largely on Git storage. Missing for 10: explicit automation version history/diff commands, a documented review/approval step for workflow changes, rollback to a prior automation version, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Workflow stores validated definitions but does not execute them.
Keep task intent, status, blockers and responses in Git-native records.
YYLO Skills are independently versioned, reusable procedures for operating YYLO and Ledger.
Review the canonical version before installation.
Save the same contract as YAML for a reusable workflow.
